newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian shares end week broadly stable.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian shares end week broadly stable.

text.p: Saudi Arabian shares ended last week broadly stable on increased turnover, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index closed at 154 points on Thursday from the previous week's 153.76 point finish. Of the 59 companies traded, 31 rose, 15 fell and 13 were unchanged.
Services sector shares dominated trade, accounting for 28 percent of volume. They were followed by industrials, which made up 24 percent of volume, and banks, with 22 percent.
BFA put turnover in the week at 4.26 million shares worth 690 million riyals ($184 million) from 2.98 million shares worth 586 million riyals the previous week.
Riyad Bank was the most active share in the week, accounting for about 20 percent of value dealt. It closed three riyals firmer at 246.

The biggest gainer in the week was Saudi Ceramics Co, which climbed 18.9 percent to 358 riyals. Earlier this month the firm said it would raise paid-up capital by 50 million riyals by issuing shareholders one new share for every three held.

Al-Ahsa Development was another big gainer, adding nearly 12 percent to 106 riyals. Saudi Industrial Development Co added over nine percent to 93 riyals and Saudi Advanced Industries Co gathered five riyals to 62. Food Products extended its recent gains, adding eight percent to 118.
Among the week's losers were Tabuk Agriculture, which fell 5.7 percent to 82 riyals. ($1=3.75 riyals)
